reader.requirement: At --std 85 the clauses of a report file's FD (BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, CODE-SET, REPORT) must be accepted in any order with the same effect (the REPORT clause ties the report wherever it stands), each written at most once; the witness covers only REPORT/LABEL/RECORD/BLOCK reversed.

edition-consulted.switches: row.At(DialectLevel) picks the figure of the edition; the FileDescriptionClauseContext row carries no Earlier figure and Sequence null (order free), so 85 reads the same figure as 2023
refuses the 2002 FORMAT clause at 85 (COBOL0900); not on the order path

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition in FileDescriptionFormats.cs (none), FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs (only the record-required and BLOCK screens, not the order path), ClauseCardinality.cs Earlier rows (FD row has none)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the order licence is the same; only the clause set differs (LABEL/VALUE OF/DATA RECORDS are 85, FORMAT is 2002+)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf22_04 reverses four clauses; VALUE OF and CODE-SET interleaved, a repeated clause and clauses outside the report format are not exercised

probes.printed: PC=01 / DONE (CODE-SET, REPORT, VALUE OF, BLOCK, LABEL, RECORD in that order)
probes.expected: accepted and the report runs: SR2 any order; INITIATE sets PAGE-COUNTER to one

probes.printed: COBOL2423 the clause 'BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS' is written 2 times
probes.expected: refused: each bracket once, order free

probes.printed: COBOL2604 the LINAGE clause is not a clause of Format 3 (report)
COBOL2604 + COBOL0900 the FORMAT clause requires COBOL-2002
PC=01 / DONE with RECORD CONTAINS 10 TO 20 CHARACTERS among the reordered clauses
COBOL6849 DATA RECORDS ZZ is not the name of an 01 record description of file 'REP-F'
probes.expected: refused (DATA RECORDS is not in the report FD format; no record may follow, SR4)

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.3.2.3 SR2  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The grammar admits fileDescriptionClause+ in any order; the format (report or not) is decided from a REPORT clause written anywhere in the entry before any clause binds, and ClosedFormatPass counts each once-only clause with no order rank. Diagnostics name §2023 sections at --std 85 (a wording matter only).

refuter.evidence: Probes in E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-165/src, run with run_probe.py --std 85. fdA.cob (VALUE OF, LABEL RECORD IS OMITTED, REPORTS ARE RPT-A RPT-B, RECORD, BLOCK 2 TO 4 RECORDS, in that order) ran: DONE, and FDA.TXT has AAAAA / '  BBBBB' / AAAAA, so a two-report REPORTS clause in the middle of the entry ties both reports. Each clause once: fdB.cob (VALUE OF twice), fdC.cob (REPORT IS twice) and fdD.cob (LABEL twice) are refused with COBOL2423. Class c: fdE.cob writes IS GLOBAL second among the report-FD clauses at 85 and runs (DONE); that is legal, because the IPC module's report-file FD (§1985:X.4.2 Format 3) prints [IS EXTERNAL] [IS GLOBAL]. ClauseCardinality.cs#ByClauseContext's FileDescriptionClauseContext row has Sequence null and no Earlier figure; the 1985 figure prints no clause the row fails to count. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.2.3 SR2  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:X.4.2.3 SR3  (4.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'.
